name: API-first companies and API providers
who: Companies whose product is the API (payments, messaging, data, infra). Seed to Series C.
pain: Docs drift from the code; every release means hand-editing reference pages; AI agents can't use the docs well.
docstar_fit: Agent-written reference from routes, GitHub drift detection, hosted MCP server + llms.txt so agents can call the API.
buyer: CTO, Head of Platform, API product owner, DevRel lead
signals: Public API reference, SDKs on npm/PyPI, changelog, no /llms.txt, no MCP server

name: SaaS companies with a public or partner API
who: B2B SaaS where the API is a secondary product used by integrators and partners.
pain: API docs are nobody's job; outdated pages create support tickets and slow partner integrations.
docstar_fit: Low-effort docs that stay in sync; try-it playground cuts support load; free plan to start.
buyer: VP Engineering, PM for integrations/platform, partnerships lead
signals: 'API' link in footer leads to PDF, Swagger UI, or a stale page; integrations marketplace

name: AI startups and AI product companies
who: Model, agent, RAG, voice and AI-infra companies selling to developers.
pain: Their own users build with agents; docs must be machine-readable (llms.txt, MCP) or they lose to competitors that are.
docstar_fit: llms.txt + markdown twin of every page, hosted MCP with OAuth, agent analytics (what agents ask, where they fail).
signals: YC/AI batch, developer API, fast-moving changelog, docs missing llms.txt or MCP

name: Companies building or shipping MCP servers
who: Teams that published an MCP server, or are asked by customers for one.
pain: Building, hosting, securing (OAuth) and documenting an MCP server is real work separate from the API.
docstar_fit: Hosted MCP server with OAuth generated from the same docs; branded MCP name; custom tools for key endpoints.
signals: Listed on MCP registries (Smithery, mcp.so, Glama); MCP repo with README-only docs

name: Companies maintaining CLIs and SDKs
who: Dev-tool and infra companies with a CLI and multiple language SDKs.
pain: Maintaining a CLI and docs for each SDK by hand; reference and CLI help drift apart.
docstar_fit: docstar-cli turns every endpoint into a terminal command (can run as local MCP); OpenAPI 3 export feeds SDK generators.
buyer: Engineering manager, DX team, tech lead
signals: Homebrew/npm CLI, several SDK repos, OpenAPI file in repo

name: Developer-tool and technical-product companies
who: Companies whose buyers are developers (observability, CI, databases, auth).
pain: Docs are the product's storefront; current platform is expensive per seat or not agent-ready.
docstar_fit: Agent-ready docs with no lock-in (OpenAPI export), white-label, $25/mo Pro vs higher per-seat tools.
signals: Docs on Mintlify/ReadMe/GitBook/Redocly; developer community

name: Companies on an existing docs platform (Segment A)
who: Anyone already on Mintlify, ReadMe, GitBook, Redocly, Docusaurus, Swagger UI or a custom site.
pain: Docs are written and updated by hand; no MCP/CLI; agent traffic invisible; cost grows with seats.
docstar_fit: Import OpenAPI/Postman in minutes, keep the site, add MCP + CLI + drift detection; export anytime.
buyer: Whoever owns docs: DevRel, DX, PM
signals: 'Powered by' footer, docs subdomain, OpenAPI file available

name: Companies with an API but no proper docs (Segment B)
who: Startups and SMBs with an API behind 'contact us', a PDF, README-only, or bare Swagger.
pain: Integrations stall; sales engineers answer the same questions; nobody has time to write docs.
docstar_fit: Paste one prompt into Claude Code/Cursor/Codex: the agent reads the routes and writes the docs. No OpenAPI file needed.
signals: 'API available on request', GitHub README as docs, old PDF reference

name: Businesses with outdated or incomplete docs
who: Docs exist but have stale examples, missing endpoints, broken links or an old changelog.
pain: Wrong docs are worse than none: failed integrations, churn, support cost.
docstar_fit: Drift detection via GitHub app drafts fixes when routes change; agents report wrong docs via MCP.
signals: Changelog last updated months ago, 404s in docs, endpoints in SDK not in docs

name: Early-stage and seed startups
who: 2-20 person technical teams launching an API or developer product.
pain: No time or budget for docs; need to look credible to first customers and investors.
docstar_fit: Free plan with unlimited pages and custom domain; docs in an afternoon; MCP and CLI from day one.
signals: Recent launch (Product Hunt, YC, Show HN), API waitlist

name: Small and medium businesses
who: Vertical SaaS and service businesses (fintech, logistics, health, e-commerce) with partner APIs.
pain: Partner onboarding depends on docs a busy engineer wrote once.
docstar_fit: Pro at $25/mo for 10 members; branded portal on own domain; try-it playground for partners.
signals: Partner/developer portal link, integration requests on site

name: Enterprise engineering and product teams
who: Large orgs with many internal and external APIs.
pain: Dozens of APIs, inconsistent docs, internal teams and agents can't discover APIs.
docstar_fit: Enterprise plan: unlimited members/collections, white-label, MCP for internal agent use, success manager.
buyer: Platform engineering director, API governance lead, CTO office
signals: API portal, internal developer platform initiatives, AI-agent rollout

name: Software development agencies
who: Agencies building APIs and integrations for clients.
pain: Docs are an unpaid afterthought at handover; clients need something professional.
docstar_fit: White-label docs, MCP and CLI under the client's brand as a billable deliverable; agent writes docs from the code.
buyer: Agency founder, delivery head, tech lead
signals: Clutch/GoodFirms listing, API development service page

name: Open-source projects and maintainers
who: OSS projects with an HTTP API or self-hosted server.
pain: README-only docs, volunteer time, contributors can't keep reference current.
docstar_fit: Free plan, GitHub Actions sync keeps docs current, llms.txt helps users' agents.
signals: Stars > 500, REST API in repo, docs issues open

name: Individual developers, indie hackers, freelancers
who: Solo builders shipping APIs, side projects and client work.
pain: Writing docs is the last thing they want to do.
docstar_fit: Free, fast, agent does the writing; looks professional; custom domain included.
signals: Indie Hackers / X build-in-public, RapidAPI listings

name: Students and technical communities
who: CS students, hackathon teams, bootcamp grads, university dev clubs.
pain: Projects without docs don't impress judges or employers.
docstar_fit: Free plan; portfolio-grade docs and an MCP server for a hackathon project in minutes.
signals: MLH hackathons, university clubs, GitHub Student Pack

name: Technical founders and product managers
who: People who own the developer experience decision.
pain: Need adoption metrics; can't see how humans vs agents use docs.
docstar_fit: Analytics split by human/agent channel: top questions, failed searches, popular endpoints.
signals: Job posts for DevRel/docs, public roadmap

name: DevRel and developer-experience teams
who: DevRel advocates, DX engineers, docs teams.
pain: Asked to make docs 'AI-ready' with no extra headcount.
docstar_fit: One-click MCP install buttons on every page, copy-prompt button, llms.txt, agent analytics.
signals: DevRel job titles, conference talks on DX

name: Developers who consume APIs through agents (demand side)
who: Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex who want their agent to find and call APIs.
pain: Agents hallucinate API usage from stale training data.
docstar_fit: Install the DocStar MCP once; agent can find, read and call any API documented on DocStar. Grows the network for publishers.
signals: Cursor/Claude Code communities, MCP directories

name: Teams with internal APIs and microservices (added)
who: Mid-size companies with many internal services and few docs.
pain: Engineers and internal AI agents can't find or trust internal API docs.
docstar_fit: Private projects, MCP so internal coding agents can call services correctly.
signals: Microservices job posts, internal developer portal talk

name: API marketplace and integration-platform sellers (added)
who: Developers selling APIs on RapidAPI/Zyla-type marketplaces, and iPaaS connector builders.
pain: Marketplace listings carry thin docs; buyers need better reference to convert.
docstar_fit: Standalone docs site + MCP that agents can discover; OpenAPI export keeps marketplace listing in sync.
signals: RapidAPI provider pages
